name: Help
explanation: Context-sensitive help needs to be available for completing tasks on the page. This means help that's relevant to the specific field or step a user is on, not just a generic help page somewhere else on the site. It can take the form of tooltips, inline hint text, a help icon next to a complex field, or a link to a specific section of documentation. Help doesn't need to be shown for every single field, only where a plain label or instruction isn't already enough on its own.
whoItAffects: People with cognitive disabilities benefit from help that's available exactly where and when they need it. Hunting through a separate general help page while also trying to remember what they were doing on the form breaks their concentration. People with limited short-term memory face a similar problem. Navigating away from a task to find help, then having to reconstruct where they left off, adds unnecessary difficulty. Context-sensitive help removes that extra step by keeping guidance attached to the specific task at hand.

codeExample.bad:
<!-- No help is available for a field that most users find confusing -->
<label for="routing">Routing number</label>
<input type="text" id="routing">
codeExample.good: What's a routing number?

howToTest: Look for form fields or steps that are commonly confusing or unfamiliar. Check whether help specific to that field or step is available nearby, such as a tooltip, hint text, or a link to a targeted explanation. If the only available help is a generic page unrelated to the specific task, or no help exists at all for a field that clearly needs it, this fails.

check.question: A tax form has a complex field labeled "Adjusted gross income" with no tooltip, hint, or link explaining what it means, though the site does have a general FAQ page elsewhere. Does this pass SC 3.3.5 Help?
choices: Yes, because a general FAQ page exists somewhere on the site
No, because context-sensitive help specific to this field isn't available where the user needs it
Yes, because tax terminology is expected to be understood by users filling out tax forms
It depends only on how long the FAQ page is
